The MBO Manufacturing Compliance team supports manufacturing operations by strengthening the quality and compliance systems used to manage deviations, corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs), change controls, and quality risk assessments. The team partners with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Digital, and other site functions to improve investigation quality, enable risk-based decisions, support inspection readiness, and drive sustainable compliance improvements across the manufacturing organization.
Role Overview
The Manufacturing Compliance AI & Automation Co-op will help design and prototype responsible AI tools that support compliance workflows. Working with compliance subject matter experts and digital partners, the Co-op will translate business needs into practical use cases, organize approved content and data, build and test AI agents, and document results. Initial use cases may include deviations, CAPAs, change controls, and risk assessments. All solutions will operate under established quality, data privacy, information security, validation, and human-review requirements.
How You Will Contribute
As a Manufacturing Compliance AI & Automation Co-op, you will have the opportunity to:
• Map current compliance workflows and identify repetitive, document-intensive activities that are appropriate for AI-assisted support.
• Gather user requirements and convert them into clear use cases, user stories, acceptance criteria, and process maps.
• Develop and test proof-of-concept AI agents for deviation investigation support, CAPA quality checks, change control impact assessment, and quality risk assessment preparation.
• Prepare and curate approved knowledge sources, example records, prompts, and test scenarios while protecting confidential and regulated information.
• Evaluate outputs for accuracy, traceability, usability, bias, and compliance risk, and document defects, limitations, and required human review.
• Build simple dashboards or summaries to communicate pilot performance, user feedback, cycle-time observations, and recommended improvements.
• Create user guides, technical documentation, governance recommendations, and a final presentation to support a sustainable handoff to the MBO Manufacturing Compliance team.
Co-op Development Opportunities
• Gain hands-on experience applying generative AI, automation, and data analytics in a regulated biopharmaceutical manufacturing environment.
• Develop practical knowledge of deviations, CAPAs, change controls, quality risk management, and Good Manufacturing Practice expectations.
• Strengthen skills in product discovery, process mapping, requirements development, prompt design, testing, validation thinking, and responsible AI governance.
• Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders and practice presenting technical concepts and recommendations to compliance professionals and leadership.
• Build a portfolio of documented prototypes and measurable business outcomes while learning how digital solutions move from concept to controlled implementation.
Job Requirements
• This position will be Hybrid (3 days per week onsite) out of the Lexington, Massachusetts location.
• Must be pursuing a Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Systems, Engineering, Bioengineering, Life Sciences, or a related field.
• Interest in generative AI, machine learning, process automation, data analytics, or digital product development.
• Working knowledge of Python, SQL, Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI, or similar tools is preferred; equivalent academic or project experience will be considered.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, documentation, and communication skills, with the ability to convert ambiguous needs into structured requirements.
• Ability to work carefully with confidential information and follow data privacy, information security, and quality-system requirements.
• Ability to collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders and incorporate feedback through iterative testing.
• Familiarity with regulated industries, Good Manufacturing Practice, quality systems, or risk management is beneficial but not required.

Hybrid Work Program
OCC operates under a Hybrid Work Program which, absent an approved exception, requires employees to work from an OCC office at least 3 days per week. About OCC:
A World Class Clearing Organization
The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) is the world's largest equity derivatives clearing organization. Founded in 1973, OCC is dedicated to promoting stability and market integrity by delivering clearing and settlement services for options, futures and securities lending transactions. As a Systemically Important Financial Market Utility (SIFMU), OCC operates under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. OCC has more than 100 clearing members and provides central counterparty (CCP) clearing and settlement services to 21 exchanges and trading platforms.
OCC also provides free and engaging educational resources about the benefits and risks of options through its Options Industry Council (OIC).
OCC is building a culture that empowers continued learning, authentic innovation, and constant creativity.
About the Intern Program:
OCC is looking for interns who are eager to learn, humble enough to ask questions, and ready to think critically about complex problems. The OCC Internship Program equips students with the real-world skills needed to transition successfully into a career in financial services. As an intern, you will contribute to meaningful projects, applying your skills and knowledge to real challenges facing the business. Your time with us is a real opportunity to make a genuine impact on the future of OCC!
OCC's Year-Round Internship Program is a 12-month opportunity running from January through December and is open to both undergraduate and graduate students who are actively enrolled at a college or university. Interns work up to 20 hours per week during the school year and up to 40 hours per week during the summer, subject to a 1,000-hour cap. The role is based in a hybrid work environment, and overtime is not permitted.
About the Team & Role
The Product & Application Security team is responsible for securing OCC's applications across their entire lifecycle, from code to production. Our work spans security testing (penetration testing, SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning), security integration into developer workflows and CI/CD pipelines, and vulnerability research and advisory. A core part of our mission is making secure development the path of least resistance for every developer at OCC.
The intern will support a key initiative: using frontier AI models to develop, codify, and embed security standards directly into OCC's developer workflows and AI-assisted coding environments. This includes building AI-consumable security configurations, automating the enforcement of security standards within our existing tooling and pipelines, and helping reduce the manual effort currently required to maintain consistency across OCC's development ecosystem. This is high-impact work that will have lasting effect on how security is practiced across the organization long after the internship concludes.
The intern will gain hands-on experience at the intersection of application security, software engineering, and frontier AI, working alongside experienced security professionals on real, production-affecting initiatives rather than isolated side projects.
Job Summary & Responsibilities
The intern will work within the Product & Application Security (AppSec) team on a high-impact initiative: using frontier AI models to research, build, and embed security standards directly into how OCC's developers write code. This is not a documentation internship. You will be using AI as a core engineering tool to codify security requirements, automate their enforcement, and embed them into developer workflows and AI-assisted coding environments across the organization.
Responsibilities include:
Using frontier AI models and LLMs as core engineering tools to research, synthesize, and codify OCC-specific secure coding standards based on industry frameworks (OWASP, NIST,CIS)
Building AI-consumable configuration files (e.g., Claude.md) that embed security requirements directly into AI-assisted developer workflows and GitHub repositories across OCC
Automating the enforcement of security standards within CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling (Snyk, SAST/DAST tools, GitHub), writing real automation that runs in production workflows

Merchandising Internship means an opportunity to explore a career as part of the world’s largest retailer! We are seeking students who exhibit curiosity, digital and financial acumen, as well as robust problem-solving skills to deliver solutions to complex and challenging issues. You will learn the core merchandising business as well as the support functions of Merchandising (such as Private Brands, Sourcing, Planning, Business Analytics, and Replenishment).  
The Internship: Held over an 11-week period during the summer of 2026 for students in their penultimate year of college. The paid internship will prepare associates for a career in Merchandising by working on a meaningful project, networking with industry experts, and developing your skills at the Fortune 1 as you explore our HQ in Northwest Arkansas!
What is Merchandising at Walmart? See below!
Data and Digital Acumen: Leverages data analysis tools to explore simple data, performs basic statistical analysis, derives insights, and creates basic reports. Uses visualization tools to represent data and construct coherent stories to influence decisions. Identifies, implements, and drives technology change within scope of work.
Shopper/Customer Experience: Owns the execution of customer communication and education programs in stores. Collaborates with the modular team. Owns search queries for an assigned category. Ensures the quality and accuracy of product page content. Follows taxonomy guidelines. Collaborates with Site Merchandising to run campaigns on the Walmart.com home page as planned. Implements rules to filter what appears in search results for shared search terms as needed.
Budgeting & Forecasting: Supports category finances by tracking performance against organizational financial targets. Creates sales reports that analyze sub-category performance against overall business results as needed. Supports forecasting as assigned.
